original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: In the abelian symmetric 2-by-2 register model with three added signed rank-one frames, prove that the eight linear symmetries permuting A, B, P, Q transport the full character table between old-count profiles; derive the exclusion of (1,1,2,0)/(1,1,1) from the cited exclusion of (2,0,1,1)/(1,1,1); reduce the sixteen census profiles still open to three orbits; and exhibit, for twelve of them, a rank-one decomposition that passes every additive character.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian native alphabet. This package stays in the abelian symmetric 2-by-2 model and answers the open question of open PR #7051 about the remaining three-frame count profiles of the census in discussion comment 19377345.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the signed-frame escape from the eight-call minimum. One more seven-call profile is excluded and no word is found, so there is no call-count saving and no selected-frontier change. The orbit reduction and the character-surviving witnesses change which argument the remaining profiles need.
stop_rule: Stop after the transport lemma, the orbit table, the transported exclusion and one character-surviving witness per orbit where one exists. Do not attempt the remaining three orbits.
evidence: PROOF.md proves the symmetry and transport lemmas. The exclusion of (1,1,2,0)/(1,1,1) is conditional on the theorem of open PR #7035 or #7051 and on the premises of PR #6190 Section 1, none replayed. verify.py checks the eight maps exactly, all 24 label permutations, residual equivariance on 35 profiles, the census orbits, both survivor tables on twelve profiles, 11264 transport comparisons, bounded box counts and six failure controls. It prints PASS_THREE_FRAME_PROFILE_ORBITS. CPython 3.12, standard library only.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Is the six-call orbit of (0,1,1,1)/(1,1,1), with R+S+T = diag(3,2), character-excluded?
open_questions.why_it_matters: One proof would close four census profiles. All 1870 box triples on 24 lines are character-excluded.
open_questions.first_step: Run the parity-image argument of PR #7035 with the form 3 x1^2 + 2 x2^2 in place of 3 x1^2 + x2^2.
open_questions.blocked_by: The constants of PR #7035 belong to diag(1,3), of determinant 3; diag(3,2) has determinant 6, so the 2-adic case split has to be redone. It was not attempted here.

open_questions.question: Does every rank-one decomposition of (2,1,1,0)/(1,1,1) fail a character or target support?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A yes answer closes the eight-profile orbit. The witness -B + (5/2)Q + (1/4)(1,3)(1,3)^T shows that characters alone cannot.
open_questions.first_step: Describe the decompositions that pass every character, starting from the lattice Z^3 + Z(1/2,1/2,1/2) of the witness, and test the subset sums for A+Q on that family.
open_questions.blocked_by: The character-surviving set is not parametrized; the box shows 82 of 1936 triples and none passes target support.

open_questions.question: Does every rank-one decomposition of (0,1,1,1)/(1,1,2) fail a character or target support?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A yes answer closes the four-profile orbit with one doubled frame. The witness (1/2)B + (1/2)(2,1)(2,1)^T + 2Q passes every character.
open_questions.first_step: Classify the index-two lattices that give a character-surviving table for R+S+2T = diag(3,2), then test the subset sums for A+P and A+Q.
open_questions.blocked_by: The doubled frame changes the call count of each character, so the three-frame argument of the predecessors does not apply as written.
